```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

class backup "Diverse-path backup WAN link" style=dashed

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub Router (Primary)"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub Router (Backup)"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary "primary WAN"
edge branch hubbackup "backup WAN" class=backup
```

Notes on how I built this:

- Genre is `topology` at `figdown 0.1` — per the router, `topology` is dispatchable at 0.1 and only carries the experimental-withdrawal risk, so no version bump or portability trade-off comment was needed.
- I did not have `reference/experimental/topology.md` or `reference/layout.md` in hand, so I used the minimal, genre-neutral `node`/`edge` vocabulary implied by the document skeleton (bare ids, quoted labels, `class=` for meaning) rather than guessing at any topology-specific keywords I haven't seen documented. Before treating this as final, run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js branch-office-wan-uplinks.fd` — if `node`/`edge` aren't the genre's actual spellings, the parser's line-numbered error will name the correct ones, per "Do not invent syntax."
- The five links/nodes named in the brief are all present: `access1`–`branch`, `access2`–`branch`, `branch`–`hubprimary`, `branch`–`hubbackup`. No extra structure was added.
- The backup link carries a `class` stating *why* it's different (diverse-path backup) rather than relying on the dashed style alone to imply meaning, per "class is how meaning survives."
